evidence: STRUCTURE (supports graded reward, no structural defect found): tests/scoring.toml has gates render=0.0/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05 (byte-identical to template; score.py and test.sh identical to template per diff). score.py computes reward = weighted mean of the three dimension scores when gates pass and functional > 0.05, so the final reward is continuous, not binary. Criterion mass (computed with tomllib): functional 43 binary criteria, total weight 58.5, individual weights 0.5-2.5 (largest single share hro_stale_refused/hro_live_board/hro_candidate_private 2.5/58.5 = 4.3%); polish 5 binary criteria totalling 12 (weights 1.5-3); visual 5 likert points=5 criteria at 1.2 each with anchors at every level. All three scored dimensions use aggregation='weighted_mean'; only the two gates use 'all_pass'. Precondition dependence: the only shared precondition is the minimal backend gate (job + candidate created by Recruiter and visible to the Observer in an independent context: gates/constraints/judge.toml:23; restated functional prompt.md:11-13, polish prompt.md:11-12, visual prompt.md:11-12). After it, functional prompt.md:13 says 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations ... When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job'. Feature clusters are separable: board moves/order/places/undo/bulk/stale (S, M, L, B, C protocols) ~ 31 weight; conversations/unread/seen/drafts (T, U) 15 weight; candidate view/privacy/link (K) 4.5; roles/anonymous (R) ~7.5; notes 1; activity 1.5; restart 1.5; live board 2.5. Polish rows are independent observations (live board preservation 3, live thread 3, earlier-place anchoring 2, failed send 1.5, session resume 2.5). Visual is 5-level craft. WEAK-APP SPREAD (reasoned, not run): (a) board-only app with moves, reorder, reject/reopen, places, no realtime, no conversations, no candidate view: functional roughly 25-30/58.5 (~0.45) -> 0.27 + visual craft ~0.1 + polish ~0 => ~0.35-0.4; (b) everything except realtime and stale-refusal: loses hro_live_board 2.5, hro_stale_refused 2.5, realtime legs of msg_exchange/unread/seen and polish live rows 6/12 => roughly 0.65-0.75; (c) golden-like app near 1.0; (d) app whose job form saves only in browser: gate 0 -> 0 (correct). This is a spread, not all-or-nothing. Refusal rows each carry their own positive control, so a do-nothing app does not earn refusal mass (relevant to discrimination, owned by rows 30/39). Plausible broken app that could pass: a server that accepts every move (no stage, places, staleness or role rules) but has a working UI would still be graded down by ~17 weight across hro_move_one_stage, hro_interview_full, hro_bulk_*, hro_stale_refused, hro_mgr_*, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous — it scores mid-range rather than full, which is the desired discrimination. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app that refuses invalid moves client-side and never sends them is protected (prompt.md:23 replays the captured successful request so server refusal is observed); an app with no Observer write controls is protected (hro_observer_readonly uses replays). No structural collapse found. RISKS / MISSING EVIDENCE: (1) raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden browser/API driver (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json; hashes re-verified) on the golden only — no mutated weak apps, no configured judge run, so the claimed spread has never been measured. REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward discrimination record before clearance. (2) Workload collapse path: functional is one batched claude-code session with 43 criteria and an 11-protocol script, judge timeout 9000 s inside scored suite budget 11100 s (test.sh:224; 9000+900+900=10800 < 11100). If the functional judge times out or errors, rewardkit produces no scored reward and test.sh:224-225 exits with score.py's gate-stage reward 0, so a partially-working (or even golden) app collapses to 0 — a real all-or-nothing failure mode whose likelihood is unmeasured. Budgets are template-identical and must not be raised automatically; this is a measurement gap, not a confirmed defect. (3) Polish is 5 binary rows; live-update-dependent rows (6/12 of polish) go to 0 together if realtime is absent — acceptable since realtime is a public requirement (instruction.md:5,7), noted only.
